Mahaneh-dan
MAH-hah-neh-DAN
n. (the camp of Dan, a place behind Kirjath-jearim named from the Danite migration)
Hebrew Machaneh Dan, the camp of Dan, from machaneh, a camp or encampment; the name stands in the text at Judges 18:12 and in the margin at Judges 13:25.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Mahaneh-dan means the camp of Dan, and it was the name given to a spot behind Kirjath-jearim where the Danite expedition halted on its way north: “And they went up, and pitched in Kirjathjearim, in Judah: wherefore they called that place Mahanehdan unto this day: behold, it is behind Kirjathjearim” (Judges 18:12). The name is a monument to a migration that should never have been necessary. Dan had been allotted an inheritance and had failed to take it: “In those days there was no king in Israel: and in those days the tribe of the Danites sought them an inheritance to dwell in; for unto that day all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes of Israel” (Judges 18:1). So six hundred armed men went out from Zorah and Eshtaol (Judges 18:11), and what they brought back from the journey was not courage but a stolen priest and a stolen idol: “And the children of Dan set up the graven image: and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land” (Judges 18:30). A camp named for a tribe became the first stage of a sanctioned idolatry that outlasted the judges and the kings. The Authorized Version also preserves the name in the margin at Judges 13:25, where the camp of Dan is where the Spirit of the LORD began to move Samson.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Mahaneh-dan is a biblical place-name and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Mahaneh-dan is the name of a place behind Kirjath-jearim; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

It stands in the text of the Authorized Version at Judges 18:12.

The Hebrew means the camp of Dan.

The same Hebrew name is given in the Authorized Version margin at Judges 13:25.

It was named from the halting of the Danite expedition toward the north.

Key Scripture

Jdg 18:12 — "And they went up, and pitched in Kirjathjearim, in Judah: wherefore they called that place Mahanehdan unto this day: behold, it is behind Kirjathjearim."

Jdg 18:1 — "In those days there was no king in Israel: and in those days the tribe of the Danites sought them an inheritance to dwell in; for unto that day all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes of Israel."

Jdg 18:11 — "And there went from thence of the family of the Danites, out of Zorah and out of Eshtaol, six hundred men appointed with weapons of war."

Jdg 18:30 — "And the children of Dan set up the graven image: and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land."

Modern Corruption

The Danite migration is told as a tribal adventure, when Judges presents it as the failure to take a given inheritance and the planting of an idolatry that lasted centuries.

expand to see more

Readers enjoy Judges 18 as a raid and miss the charge in it. Dan had an inheritance by lot and did not possess it; rather than fight for what God had given, the tribe went looking for easier ground, and on the way it acquired a priest for hire and a carved image. The result is named in the chapter itself: priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land. Unbelief that looks like enterprise is still unbelief.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that a people who will not take the inheritance God assigned will take something else instead, and that what they take will usually be an idol.
